labeling.note: Held-out semantic set for the 2026-09-09 utility round (round 3). Eighteen feature/overview/call-chain/issue-style requests over the four round-2 held-out repositories (click, fastify, chi, jsoup), which no semantic, CSN or issue suite has used. Relevant files and grades were written from a read of each repository's source before any round-3 code change was measured and were never compared against retrieval output. The manifest hash is recorded in the round report and the suite is run once per side at the end of the round.

cases.query: Explain how click parses command-line arguments: from Command.main creating a Context, through the option parser, to converting parameter values with their types.
cases.rationale: Command/Context live in core.py, the parser in parser.py, value conversion in types.py.

cases.query: How does click implement shell tab completion for commands, options, and their values?
cases.rationale: Completion classes and the entry point are in shell_completion.py; Command/Parameter and ParamType provide shell_complete hooks.

cases.query: How does click render the --help page: the usage line, the options table, and the list of subcommands with text wrapping?
cases.rationale: HelpFormatter in formatting.py renders sections; Command/Group in core.py assemble usage, options and command lists.

cases.query: Trace click.echo from writing a message to resolving the output stream and stripping ANSI color codes when the stream is not a terminal.
cases.rationale: echo lives in utils.py and delegates stream resolution and ANSI handling to _compat.py; Windows console streams are in _winconsole.py.
Choice.convert in types.py normalises and returns the value; Parameter.process_value in core.py invokes the conversion.

cases.query: Explain fastify's request lifecycle from the HTTP server accepting a request, through routing and the onRequest and preHandler hooks, to the handler and reply serialization.
cases.rationale: route.js registers routes and the router handler, handle-request.js runs the hook/handler sequence, hooks.js runs hooks, reply.js serializes and sends, server.js creates the server.

cases.query: How does fastify compile a route's JSON schemas into validators and validate the incoming body, querystring, params, and headers?
cases.rationale: validation.js compiles and runs validators; schema-controller.js owns the compilers and shared schemas; route.js triggers compilation; schemas.js normalises schema shapes.

cases.query: How does fastify parse request bodies by content type and where are the default JSON and plain text parsers registered?
cases.rationale: ContentTypeParser in content-type-parser.js holds the parsers and default JSON/text parsers; content-type.js parses the header; fastify.js constructs the parser.

cases.query: Trace reply.send from a JavaScript object payload through the preSerialization and onSend hooks and the route's serializer to writing the response.
cases.rationale: Reply.send and the serialization steps are in reply.js; the onSend/preSerialization runners in hooks.js; the serializer compiler is owned by schema-controller.js.

cases.query:
exposeHeadRoute registers a HEAD route even when the plugin already declared one for the same path

With `exposeHeadRoutes: true` (the default) a plugin that declares both `GET /items` and `HEAD /items` fails at startup with a duplicate route error for `HEAD /items`. Expected: when a HEAD route for the path already exists, fastify should skip the automatic HEAD route instead of adding it twice.

```js
fastify.get('/items', handler)
fastify.head('/items', headHandler)
```
cases.rationale: route.js decides whether to add the automatic HEAD route; head-route.js holds the automatic HEAD onSend handler.

cases.query: Explain how chi routes an incoming request: from Mux.ServeHTTP through the middleware chain and the radix tree lookup to the route context that exposes URL parameters.
cases.rationale: Mux in mux.go, radix tree in tree.go, route Context in context.go, middleware chaining in chain.go.

cases.query: How does chi match route patterns with named parameters, regular expressions, and wildcards against the request path?
cases.rationale: Pattern segmentation and matching are in tree.go; matched parameters are stored on the Context; Mux drives the lookup.

cases.query: Trace how Mux.Mount attaches a sub-router and how a request is dispatched into it with the remaining route path.
cases.rationale: Mount and the mount handler are in mux.go; the route path and pattern bookkeeping in context.go; the tree stores the wildcard mount node.

cases.query:
Compress middleware keeps the original Content-Length header after compressing the body

When a handler sets `Content-Length` explicitly before writing and the response goes through `middleware.Compress`, the client receives the compressed body with the uncompressed length, so the body is truncated or the connection is held open.

```go
r.Use(middleware.Compress(5))
r.Get("/", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    w.Header().Set("Content-Length", strconv.Itoa(len(payload)))
    w.Write(payload)
})
```

Expected: the compressing writer removes or rewrites Content-Length when it decides to compress.
cases.rationale: The compressing response writer in compress.go decides when to compress and touches headers; wrap_writer.go provides the wrapped writer it builds on.

cases.query: Explain jsoup's HTML parsing architecture: how the tokeniser turns characters into tokens, how the tree builder state machine consumes them, and how the Document tree is assembled.
cases.rationale: Tokeniser/TokeniserState produce tokens, HtmlTreeBuilder/HtmlTreeBuilderState insert nodes, TreeBuilder is the shared driver and Parser the entry point.

cases.query: How does jsoup evaluate a CSS selector: parsing the query string into Evaluator objects and collecting the matching elements from the tree?
cases.rationale: QueryParser builds Evaluators, Evaluator implements matching, Selector is the entry point, Collector walks the tree, StructuralEvaluator covers combinators.

cases.query: Trace Jsoup.connect(url).get() from the Connection builder through HttpConnection executing the request to parsing the response body into a Document.
cases.rationale: Jsoup.connect creates an HttpConnection; HttpConnection.get executes and parses via DataUtil.parseInputStream; Connection is the interface.

cases.query:
Element.text() collapses whitespace inside 
 blocks

Calling `text()` on an element that contains a `
` child returns the preformatted content with runs of spaces and newlines collapsed to single spaces, so indentation in code samples is lost.

```java
Document doc = Jsoup.parse("
  line 1\n    line 2
");
System.out.println(doc.select("div").first().text());
```

Expected: whitespace inside `
` (and other whitespace-preserving tags) is kept as in the source, as `wholeText()` does.
cases.rationale: Element.text and appendNormalisedText decide when to preserve whitespace; StringUtil.appendNormalisedWhitespace does the collapsing; TextNode holds the text.
